biggest_catch: Stepes publishes NO pay rates — compensation is disclosed only per-project inside the workflow, so you apply, qualify, and wait with zero visibility into what any job pays until a specific project offer arrives.
catches: No official published pay rate or pay scale anywhere on stepes.com/translators — the page only says to 'Review ... compensation terms before accepting work' on a per-project basis.

Zero guaranteed work: the official page states 'Submitting an application does not guarantee acceptance, immediate review, or project assignments' and 'Project availability is not guaranteed and varies according to business demand.'
Qualification review is required — profile, résumé, credentials, and demand-alignment screening before any assignment consideration.

Work is professional/enterprise-focused (life sciences, legal, regulated content) — casual or inexperienced translators are unlikely to qualify; relevant experience, education, and CAT-tool readiness are expected.
Variable gig work, never fixed income; effective hourly pay depends on undisclosed per-project rates.
Stepes contacts applicants only 'when their qualifications align with current or anticipated business needs' — you can wait indefinitely.

c1.evidence: Stepes is a real operating translation company (professional translation platform; official page stepes.com/translators/ loaded live with full linguist-program detail).

c2.evidence: FAIL — no official page states a pay figure or a public pay mechanism. The official line is only: 'Review the languages, content type, service requirements, subject matter, schedule, file format, quality expectations, and compensation terms before accepting work.'

c3.evidence: No upfront fee — applying is free; the page lists only profile creation, qualification review, and onboarding/compliance.

c4.evidence: FAIL — no official statement of payout timing, method, or minimums; compensation terms are revealed per project inside the workflow.

eligibility: Professional translators and qualified language specialists: native or near-native target-language command, relevant experience (translation, editing, localization, interpreting, MTPE, multilingual AI evaluation), appropriate education/certifications, CAT-tool and translation-memory readiness, and professional conduct. Applying does not guarantee acceptance or any assignments.
notes: Read stepes.com/translators/ (live 2026-09-23): full 'Become a Translator' page — create professional profile, submit qualifications, complete qualification review, finish onboarding/compliance, be considered for project matching. Key official quotes: 'Submitting an application or creating a profile does not guarantee acceptance, immediate review, or project assignments' and 'Project availability is not guaranteed and varies according to business demand.' No rates, no payout method, no minimums, no timing published. Verdict 'reject': no official published pay figure or public mechanism. Could NOT confirm: any per-word/hour/task rate, payout method or minimums, how long qualification review takes, or whether a translator mobile app exists (left null).
